semester: 4th or 6th semester, annually in winter semester

learning_outcomes.text: Students know the basic concepts and terms of game theory, including strategic games, extensive games, and coalition games.
They understand and can apply and prove central theorems of game theory.
They are able to apply game-theoretic models to real problems, solve them, and evaluate the results.
Students are able to work effectively in groups and develop common solutions for game-theoretic problems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Game Theory: Historical development, fields of application, basic concepts
Static Games: Dominant strategies, Nash equilibrium, efficiency
Dynamic Games: Tree representation, backward induction, subgame perfect equilibrium
Cooperative Games: Coalition formation, Shapley value
Bayesian Games: Incomplete information, Bayesian equilibrium
Evolutionary Game Theory: Replicator equations, evolutionarily stable strategies
teaching_methods: seminar-style instruction with active exercise components

assessment_methods.method: combination exam (project work and oral exam)

assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded for passing the module examination. The grading's weight for the final grade is according to the study and examination regulations (SPO).
